title: Yara and the Uniform
premise: Yara Crane has spent their nineteen years cutting punches and casting type in their father's workshop in the river town of Vellmarch, convinced that history is something printed in distant capitals, never lived at home. When the army requisitions the town on the eve of revolution, they also seize the workshop's master ledger — a register of every citizen's name, debts, and loyalties — intending to rewrite it and erase the town's claims to its own past. Yara and a handful of printers, apprentices, and neighbors must finish setting and secretly printing the true ledger before the requisition order destroys the workshop and the original records with it. The book ends with Yara pulling the last printed sheet as soldiers breach the doors, the workshop burning behind them, the true ledger carried into the revolution by the very people it names.
about_author: Sable Amberdale is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in provincial archives. Their fiction is drawn from marginalia, apprenticeship ledgers, and the quiet lives of tradespeople caught in history's margins.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A day in the workshop: cutting a punch for the letter 'R', banter with the apprentices, their father Aldous's strictures about the ledger's sanctity. Yara dismisses talk of coming unrest as city gossip. Emotional beat: the comfort of craft, and the reader's first hint that the ledger holds more than accounts.

chapters.title: Boots on the Cobblestones
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Soldiers march into Vellmarch at dusk; a requisition notice is nailed to the workshop door claiming all presses, records, and 'persons of trade' for state service. Aldous goes pale at the clause about ledgers. Emotional beat: the safe rhythm of the shop shatters; Yara feels history arrive like weather.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. He shows Yara the master ledger: names, debts, land claims, and testimonies going back four generations — legal proof of the townspeople's rights. The army wants it 'corrected.' Emotional beat: inheritance revealed; Aldous's fear that a lifetime's work will be erased in a day.

chapters.title: The Commissar's Ink
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Commissar Voss inspects the shop, courteous and chilling, ordering a 'revised edition' of the ledger printed by month's end — with names struck out. He compliments Yara's type-cutting. Emotional beat: the horror of one's own craft turned into an instrument of erasure.

chapters.title: Apprentices' Oath
chapters.summary: Tamsin, the eldest apprentice, narrates. She gathers the workshop's workers in the type cellar and proposes printing the true ledger in secret, in parallel with Voss's false one. Not everyone agrees. Emotional beat: fear vs. loyalty; the fragile birth of a conspiracy of compositors.

chapters.title: Learning the Enemy's Schedule
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara volunteers to serve Voss's printing detail to learn deadlines, paper supplies, and which pages will be struck. They copy the false ledger's structure from memory each night. Emotional beat: guilt and double life; Yara's hands shake setting the first struck name.

chapters.title: Paper Is a Country
chapters.summary: Merchant Odile Ferrand's POV. She controls the town's paper supply and must decide whether to divert stock to the secret print run, risking her family's safety. Emotional beat: a pragmatic woman choosing memory over survival arithmetic.

chapters.title: The First Proof
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Night work in the cellar: the first true pages pulled, still warm, smelling of ink. A near-miss when a soldier knocks at the door mid-print. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror fused; the printed page becomes an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Names We Cannot Lose
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The team debates whose names matter if they run out of time — a brutal triage of the town's memory. Yara insists on including the poor and the disgraced. Emotional beat: ethics of remembrance; Yara claims the inheritance as theirs.

chapters.title: Aldous's Hands
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. His tremor worsens; he can no longer cut punches. He teaches Yara the master's cuts in a single long night, passing on techniques he swore he'd teach 'when there was time.' Emotional beat: mortality and transmission; a father finishing his work through his child.

chapters.title: Voss's Dinner Party
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Summoned to dine at the requisitioned mayor's house, Yara must charm Voss while overhearing that the workshop will be burned 'with the records' after printing. Emotional beat: dread crystallizes into a deadline — weeks, not months.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Someone in town is feeding the army details; suspicion falls on the workshop. Odile sets a trap using false paper shipments. Emotional beat: paranoia inside the conspiracy; trust becomes the scarcest resource.

chapters.title: Fire in the Type Cellar
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A 'accidental' fire damages part of the secret stock and nearly kills the youngest apprentice, Pip. The informer is exposed — not a traitor, but a terrified boy coerced by soldiers. Emotional beat: grief, mercy, and the cost of the choice to resist.

chapters.title: Two Ledgers, One Press
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The schedule tightens: days printing the false ledger for Voss by daylight, the true one by night. Yara begins to blur the two, slipping true names into the false edition's margins. Emotional beat: quiet sabotage; craft as resistance.

chapters.title: The Revolution Reaches the River
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs (Pip, Odile, a soldier). News arrives of uprisings downstream; the army grows nervous, moves up the destruction date. Townsfolk begin openly gathering. Emotional beat: history stops being something that happens elsewhere — the town realizes it is the story.

chapters.title: What Voss Knows
chapters.summary: Voss's POV, the only chapter from the antagonist. He has known about the secret printing for some time and has let it continue — a test, a trap, or a private doubt. Emotional beat: the enemy revealed as a believer in order, not a monster; the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Last Form
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. With soldiers at the edge of the square, the team sets the final pages — the town's names, Aldous's testimony, Yara's own name last. Aldous locks the original ledger inside a press forme as a mold. Emotional beat: solemnity; printing as a sacrament of memory.

chapters.title: Night of the Pull
chapters.summary: Yara and Tamsin's alternating POV. The full print run through the night as the army advances; pages distributed to runners — Odile's carts, Pip's rooftops. Voss arrives at the door with soldiers. Emotional beat: breathless climax; every pull of the lever a heartbeat.

chapters.title: The Workshop Stands, Then Falls
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Confrontation with Voss among the presses; Aldous refuses to leave and stays with his workshop as it is put to the torch. Yara escapes through the paper store with the master copy. Emotional beat: devastating loss and unbreakable purpose entwined.

chapters.title: Ash on the River
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The town wakes to smoke and to the printed ledger in every doorway, window, and hand. The false edition becomes worthless overnight; soldiers desert as the uprising arrives to find a town that already knows its own name. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into collective strength.

chapters.title: What We Set in Metal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, weeks later. In the ruins, Yara salvages punches from the ashes — the letter 'R' among them — and begins teaching other survivors to cut type. Voss is gone; his fate left uncertain. Emotional beat: mourning Aldous; inheritance accepted and renewed.

chapters.title: The First Impression
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A new press rises in the market hall; the first sheet off it is the ledger's opening page, printed for everyone. Yara sets a dedication to their father and to 'all who were named.' Emotional beat: resolution — belonging forged in ink, memory as the town's true inheritance, history now unmistakably theirs.
